name: H-Mem

paper.title: H-Mem: A Novel Memory Mechanism for Evolving and Retrieving Agent Memory via a Hybrid Structure

construction.unit: memory event extracted per fragment; fragments and summaries also stored
construction.kept_as: extracted events + verbatim fragments + LLM summaries
construction.processing: LLM event extraction; LLM entity/relation extraction (spaCy NER fallback); parent summaries
construction.writer: LLM via extraction/consolidation prompts (App. C.1); backbones GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4.1-mini

organization.stores: tree (day/week/month/year levels); entity graph with salient-entity profiles
organization.index: Qwen3-Embedding-4B vectors for fragments/events/summaries; lexical entity matching

management.operations: join similar cluster in time window, regenerate parent summary; merge entities/relations
management.forgetting: no deletion described; Ebbinghaus decay (tau 365 days) only as ranking prior

retrieval.query: LLM decomposes into dependent sub-queries with Short/Long/Mixed scope, time hints
retrieval.candidates: lexical+vector entity seeds, multi-hop graph expansion, bottom-up tree search
retrieval.budget: top-k candidates; default k not stated (k 5-50 tested, k=30 variant)

use.context: ranked evidence chain per sub-query plus prerequisite sub-answers
use.reasoning: sub-answer per sub-query, LLM synthesis; missing-info follow-up query

stages.ingestion: Original memory fragments (speaker, timestamp, conversation text) are kept; an LLM extracts one or more fine-grained memory events from each fragment.
stages.construction: Each event becomes a leaf of a temporal-semantic tree; in parallel an LLM extracts entities and relations per fragment, which are normalised/disambiguated (lemmatisation, token overlap, fuzzy match; spaCy NER fallback) into a knowledge graph whose entity nodes link back to source fragments.
stages.organization: Hybrid structure: a 4-level tree (day/week/month/year windows) whose upper nodes hold LLM summaries of semantically similar children within the same time window (thresholds 0.8/0.7/0.6), plus an entity-relation knowledge graph with profiles for salient entities; embeddings kept for fragments, events and summaries.
stages.update: Incremental bottom-up insertion: a new node joins a similar cluster in its time window (parent summary regenerated) or gets a new parent; graph entities merge on exact/fuzzy match and duplicate relations merge evidence. A consolidation count and last-consolidation time feed an Ebbinghaus-style robustness score.
stages.retrieval: An LLM decomposes the query into dependent sub-queries, each labelled Short/Long/Mixed scope with temporal hints; seed entities are found by lexical + vector matching, expanded multi-hop in the graph, mapped to fragments/events, then the tree is searched bottom-up; evidence is ranked by 0.70*semantic + 0.15*temporal + 0.15*robustness and reranked (Qwen3-Reranker-4B); a missing-information follow-up query fires when first-pass evidence is insufficient.
stages.answer: A sub-answer is generated per sub-query (using prerequisite sub-answers as context) and an LLM synthesises the final answer.

summary: Couples a temporal-semantic summary tree (short-term events consolidating into long-term summaries by time window) with an entity knowledge graph, and retrieves over both with LLM query decomposition and a time/robustness-aware evidence score.
notes:
AXES CORRECTED from the paper; earlier taxonomy row was: turn | verbatim | write-time filter | dual tree | FAISS + LCA expansion (vector). AXES-CHECK: the seed taxonomy row (turn / verbatim / write-time filter / dual tree / FAISS + LCA expansion) does not match arXiv 2605.15701 and may describe a different H-Mem paper (e.g. 2507.22925). In 2605.15701: leaf unit is an LLM-extracted memory event (original fragments are also kept and retrievable); no write-time filter is described; organisation is one temporal-semantic tree plus an entity knowledge graph (not a dual tree); selection is LLM sub-query planning + lexical/vector entity seeding + multi-hop graph expansion + bottom-up tree search + reranking, with no FAISS or LCA mention. No code URL is given in the paper. Backbones in experiments: GPT-4o-mini and GPT-4.1-mini; embedding Qwen3-Embedding-4B, reranker Qwen3-Reranker-4B (Appendix A.2).
DESIGN: Sec 3.1-3.3, Sec 4.1, App. A.2-A.4, App. C (prompt titles only).
